scenario.title: Defect Issue Triage and Risk Reporting
scenario.initial_description: When a defect occurs, the engineer reports it, discusses it with related teams, performs additional experiments, and decides how to improve the issue and communicate the risk.

reference_workflow.goal: Triage a defect issue, coordinate investigation, and report improvement actions and customer risk.

activities.name: Register defect issue with initial evidence
Classify issue severity and affected scope
Notify related teams and assign owners
Review experiment result and select improvement action
Share final report and action items

decisions.condition: Does the experiment support the root-cause hypothesis?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Issue reports can be pre-structured from defect descriptions and evidence attachments.
Related teams can be suggested from issue category and affected process area.
Action-item extraction and risk report drafting can be partially automated.

decisions.condition: Is the defect severity critical enough to escalate immediately?

branches.label: Yes - Critical
branches.description: Immediately convene cross-team meeting and notify senior stakeholders

branches.label: No - Non-critical
branches.description: Follow standard submission and triage process

decisions.condition: Do additional experiments provide sufficient root cause clarity?
Is the risk level above the reporting threshold?

branches.label: Yes - Above threshold
branches.description: Publish formal risk report and notify all stakeholders

branches.label: No - Below threshold
branches.description: Document internally and proceed to resolution monitoring

exceptions.description: Defect cannot be reproduced during additional experimentation
exceptions.trigger: Experiment results inconclusive after multiple attempts
exceptions.handling: Escalate to senior engineering review; document as intermittent defect; apply conservative risk classification

exceptions.description: Required team members unavailable for cross-team discussion
exceptions.trigger: Key stakeholders do not respond within defined SLA
exceptions.handling: Escalate to team lead; schedule asynchronous review; flag delay in defect tracking system

exceptions.description: Risk report rejected or disputed by receiving stakeholder
exceptions.trigger: Stakeholder raises objection to risk classification or findings
exceptions.handling: Initiate review cycle; document dispute; reconvene risk assessment meeting

exceptions.trigger: Defect recurs after implementation of improvement plan
exceptions.handling: Reopen defect report; return to cross-team discussion phase; update risk classification

automation_opportunities.target: A1 - Defect Detection and Initial Reporting
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated monitoring tools can detect anomalies in process or test data and pre-populate defect report fields, reducing manual effort and improving detection speed.
constraints: Requires standardized data formats from upstream systems
False positive rate must be validated before deployment

automation_opportunities.rationale: Submission and routing of defect reports can be automated based on defect type, severity, and team assignment rules, eliminating manual routing delays.
constraints: Assignment rules must be maintained and kept current
Edge cases may still require manual override

automation_opportunities.rationale: Rule-based or ML-based classification can determine severity and trigger escalation automatically based on predefined thresholds and historical defect patterns.
constraints: Initial model training requires labeled historical data
Human override capability must be preserved for novel defect types

automation_opportunities.rationale: Meeting scheduling and asynchronous collaboration can be partially automated via calendar integration and structured discussion templates, though human judgment remains central.
constraints: Full automation of discussion content is not feasible
Cultural and organizational norms may limit automation adoption

automation_opportunities.rationale: Risk scoring algorithms can be applied to structured defect and experiment data to produce draft risk classifications, accelerating the assessment step.
constraints: Regulatory compliance may require human sign-off on final classification
Model must be auditable and explainable

automation_opportunities.rationale: Generation and distribution of standardized risk reports can be automated using templates populated from the risk management system, with conditional routing based on risk level.
constraints: Report content requiring narrative judgment must remain human-authored
Audit trail requirements must be satisfied by automated system

automation_opportunities.target: A8 - Defect Resolution Monitoring and Closure
automation_opportunities.rationale: Status tracking and SLA monitoring for corrective action completion can be automated, with automated alerts triggered when milestones are missed or validation tests are executed.
constraints: Final closure approval should remain a human activity
Integration with laboratory or test systems required for automated result ingestion

assumptions: A defect tracking system exists and is accessible to all relevant actors for logging and status updates.
Cross-team discussions are assumed to be synchronous meetings or structured asynchronous reviews, not informal ad-hoc conversations.
Additional experimentation refers to controlled tests or analyses performed by the engineer, not external third-party testing.
Risk reporting is assumed to follow an internal threshold-based framework that determines when external or senior communication is required.
The improvement strategy may include process changes, design modifications, or operational controls, but the specific domain is not assumed.
Defect closure requires validation evidence confirming the corrective action has resolved the issue.
Actors labeled as 'Related Teams' are assumed to vary by defect type and are determined at the time of cross-team discussion.
The workflow is assumed to be linear with defined feedback loops at the experimentation and closure stages, not a parallel multi-stream process.
No specific regulatory framework is assumed, but compliance considerations are noted as a constraint where relevant.
